summary.en: A free, year-long sustainability leadership programme by Masdar's Youth 4 Sustainability platform for UAE high-school students aged 15–18. Ambassadors train on the SDGs, work at major events such as Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week and build AI apps in the Code 4 Climate hackathon.

Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week) და Code 4 Climate ჰაკათონზე AI აპლიკაციებს ქმნიან.
summary.ar: برنامج مجاني لمدة عام لقيادة الاستدامة تقدّمه منصة شباب من أجل الاستدامة التابعة لمصدر لطلاب المدارس الثانوية في الإمارات بعمر 15–18 عامًا. يتدرّب السفراء على أهداف التنمية المستدامة ويشاركون في فعاليات كبرى مثل أسبوع أبوظبي للاستدامة ويطوّرون تطبيقات ذكاء اصطناعي في هاكاثون Code 4 Climate.

about.en:
The Sustainability Ambassadors Program is Masdar's flagship school-age track within Youth 4 Sustainability (Y4S). It runs for 12 months, starting at Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week (ADSW) each January, and mixes online sessions, in-person and virtual events, the Y4S Annual Forum & Hub and the Sustainability Leadership Series.

Ambassadors receive core training on the UN Sustainable Development Goals, gain hands-on experience and networking at major sustainability events, and take part in the Innovation Lab, including Code 4 Climate, a two-day hackathon in which teams build AI-enabled mobile apps that tackle the SDGs. They also represent Y4S in their schools.

The programme is completely free (Y4S states it will never ask participants to pay). It is for UAE nationals or residents aged 15–18 who attend a UAE school and speak excellent English. Applications (video, personal statement and short questions) close on 30 November; selections are announced in January.

en: Free, 12-month programme starting at Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week
Code 4 Climate AI app hackathon and Innovation Lab
Networking at the region's largest sustainability events

eligibility.en: UAE nationals or residents aged 15–18 enrolled in a UAE-based school, with excellent spoken English and a genuine interest in sustainability. Must commit to attending all series and events, including ADSW.

en: Open the Sustainability Ambassadors page on y4s.ae
Register on the Y4S portal
Record and upload a short video
Write a personal statement on why you want to join and answer the personal questions
Submit before 30 November and wait for January selection results

costs.en: Free. No fees of any kind; participants attend events in Abu Dhabi.

score_reason: Free, prestigious year-long programme for UAE school students; deadline 30 Nov 2026.

summary.en: Masdar's free, year-long Future Sustainability Leaders programme connects university students and young professionals aged 19–35 with sustainability leaders, mentors and employers. International participants are accepted and do not need to live in the UAE.
summary.ka: Masdar-ის უფასო, ერთწლიანი პროგრამა Future Sustainability Leaders 19–35 წლის სტუდენტებსა და ახალგაზრდა პროფესიონალებს მდგრადობის ლიდერებთან, მენტორებთან და დამსაქმებლებთან აკავშირებს. მიიღება საერთაშორისო მონაწილეებიც, არაბთა საამიროებში ცხოვრება საჭირო არ არის.
summary.ar: برنامج مجاني لمدة عام من مصدر يربط طلاب الجامعات والمهنيين الشباب بعمر 19–35 عامًا بقادة الاستدامة والمرشدين وأصحاب العمل. يُقبل المشاركون الدوليون ولا يُشترط الإقامة في الإمارات.

about.en:
Future Sustainability Leaders (FSL) is the university and young-professional track of Masdar's Youth 4 Sustainability platform. It lasts 12 months and starts each January at Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week (ADSW), followed by online and in-person activities through the year.

Participants get one-to-one mentoring, Talent Connect career dialogues with internship and entry-level pathways, access to the Y4S Annual Forum & Hub and Sustainability Leadership Series, and the Out-of-Labs innovation challenge. Any major is welcome.

The programme is free. It is open to UAE nationals and international students aged 19–35 who hold or are pursuing an undergraduate degree and speak excellent English; living in the UAE is not required, and the programme has accepted participants from many countries. Apply with a video, personal statement and short questions by 30 November.

en: Free and open to international applicants
One-to-one mentorship and Talent Connect career pathways
Starts at Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week

eligibility.en: Aged 19–35; UAE nationals or international students holding or pursuing an undergraduate degree at an accredited institution (any major); excellent spoken English. UAE residence not required, but attendance at ADSW and all virtual series is expected.

Register on the FSL portal
Upload a short video and a personal statement
Answer the personal questions and submit by 30 November
Selections are announced in January

costs.en: Free; Y4S never charges participants. Travel to Abu Dhabi for ADSW is not stated as covered.

score_reason: Free, open to international students, strong network; deadline 30 Nov 2026.

summary.ar: جولة إقليمية من كأس العالم للباحثين في دبي، تتنافس فيها فرق من ثلاثة طلاب في المناظرة والكتابة والمسابقات وتحدي الباحث وفق منهج متعدد التخصصات. تتأهل الفرق المتفوقة إلى الجولة العالمية وبطولة الأبطال في جامعة ييل.

about.en:
The World Scholar's Cup (WSC) is an international academic tournament for school students built around a yearly interdisciplinary theme. The Dubai March Round runs 27–29 March 2027, with days 1–2 at Sunmarke School and day 3 at Arcadia Global School.

Teams of three compete in team debate, collaborative writing, the Scholar's Challenge (individual multiple-choice) and the Scholar's Bowl quiz, followed by awards and social events. Students compete in Junior or Senior divisions and can qualify for a Global Round and then the Tournament of Champions at Yale University.

Any school student can take part; schools usually register teams, but independent teams are accepted. Fees are set per round and shown in the WSC registration system.

en: Debate, writing, quiz and Scholar's Challenge in one event
Qualification path to Global Rounds and the Tournament of Champions at Yale
Friendly format for first-time competitors

eligibility.en: School students of any nationality in the Junior or Senior division age bands set by WSC; teams of three (schools or independent teams).

en: Open the Dubai March Round page on scholarscup.org
Request information or log in to the WSC registration system
Form a team of three and register for the round
Pay the round fee and study the year's curriculum

costs.en: Registration fee per student set by WSC for the round (see registration system); travel and accommodation at participants' own cost.

score_reason: Popular, accessible academic competition with an international pathway; paid.

summary.ka: World Scholar's Cup-ის 2027 წლის მეორე რეგიონული რაუნდი დუბაიში: გუნდური დებატები, ერთობლივი წერა, Scholar's Challenge და Scholar's Bowl. ძლიერი გუნდები გლობალურ რაუნდებსა და Tournament of Champions-ზე გადიან.

about.en:
The Dubai May Round of the World Scholar's Cup takes place 29–31 May 2027 at Sunmarke School and Arcadia Global School. It follows the same format as every WSC round and uses the current season's interdisciplinary curriculum.

Teams of three take part in team debate, collaborative writing, the individual Scholar's Challenge and the Scholar's Bowl, with awards ceremonies and a scholar's ball. Results can qualify students for a summer Global Round and then the Tournament of Champions at Yale.

It suits students who missed the March round or want a second attempt at qualification. Registration and fees are handled through the WSC registration system.

en: Late-season chance to qualify for the Global Round
Interdisciplinary curriculum covering science, history, art and more
Welcoming to new and returning teams

eligibility.en: School students in WSC Junior or Senior divisions, any nationality; teams of three.

en: Open the WSC calendar and choose the Dubai May Round
Request info or log in to registration.scholarscup.org
Register your team of three and pay the fee
Prepare using the season's curriculum guide

costs.en: Per-student round fee set by WSC; travel and accommodation not included.

score_reason: Accessible academic competition with qualification path; paid.

summary.en: A fully funded KAUST Academy track for Saudi university students in renewable energy and storage: online Coursera prerequisites, a December placement test, two in-person lecture weeks and an 8-week summer programme at a partner institution. Registration closes 5 November.

about.en:
The Energy Transition Specialization is one of KAUST Academy's four university specializations. Stage 1 is self-paced Coursera prerequisites (general chemistry, materials science, mechanics, electric fields), followed by a placement test in December, two in-person lecture stages (Renewable Energy & Storage I and II) during university breaks, and an 8-week summer programme at a KAUST Academy partner institution in Saudi Arabia or abroad with on-campus accommodation.

Students advance only by passing the assessment after each stage. Those not selected for the in-person stages keep Coursera access and can earn free certificates.

It is offered on a full scholarship to Saudi nationals (or children of Saudi citizens) aged 21–30 in years 3–5 of a Saudi university, or graduated within two years in an energy-relevant field. Apply by the online form before 5 November.

en: Full scholarship including summer programme accommodation
Hands-on renewable energy and storage curriculum from KAUST
Free Coursera certificates for all admitted to stage 1

eligibility.en: Saudi nationals or children of Saudi citizens, aged 21–30, in the 3rd–5th year at a Saudi university or graduated within the last two years in an energy-relevant field.

en: Read the programme page on academy.kaust.edu.sa
Submit the 2026–2027 application form before 5 November
Enrol in the Coursera prerequisites within 3 days of the invitation
Take the December placement test
Pass each stage assessment to advance

costs.en: Full scholarship: no tuition, Coursera access included, summer accommodation provided.

score_reason: Fully funded KAUST training, Saudi-only; deadline 5 Nov 2026.

summary.ar: برنامج بحثي صيفي لمدة ستة أسابيع في كاوست لأفضل طلاب الصف الحادي عشر السعوديين، يعملون فيه داخل مختبرات أعضاء هيئة التدريس مع مرشدين إلى جانب مقررات وأنشطة إثرائية.

about.en:
The Saudi Research Science Institute (SRSI) brings high-achieving high-school students to KAUST each summer for six weeks of real STEM research. Participants are placed in KAUST faculty labs, supported by mentors, and also take coursework and enrichment activities, finishing with research presentations.

It is only for Saudi national students in grade 11. The application covers biography, academic history and essays on motivation, research interests and extracurriculars, plus two recommendation letters (in English) from maths or science teachers, a 200 SAR non-refundable application fee and an online interview for eligible candidates.

In the 2026 cycle the deadline was 15 January; the 2027 cycle is expected to follow the same pattern, so prepare essays and recommenders in November–December.

en: Six weeks of real research in KAUST labs
Mentored by KAUST faculty and researchers
One of the most selective pre-university STEM programmes in Saudi Arabia

eligibility.en: Saudi national students in grade 11 with strong maths and science records.

en: Read the SRSI page and application process on academy.kaust.edu.sa
Create an account on the KAUST portal and complete the online application
Ask two maths/science teachers to submit English recommendation letters
Pay the 200 SAR application fee
Attend the online interview if shortlisted

costs.en: 200 SAR non-refundable application fee; programme cost coverage not stated on the page (historically residential at KAUST).

score_reason: Elite research summer for Saudi grade-11 students; next deadline ~Jan 2027.

about.en:
Women in STEM is a KAUST Academy programme that prepares Saudi women for graduate study and STEM careers. Over 15 months it combines in-person periods at KAUST with online learning aligned to the Saudi academic calendar, covering STEM training, standardised-test preparation, soft skills and academic mentorship.

It is open to female Saudi seniors and fresh graduates with a bachelor's in a STEM field. There is no minimum GPA and no TOEFL/IELTS requirement; admission is by a two-part admissions test (STEM and English, one hour each) and a personal interview.

The programme is free, including accommodation and meals during in-person periods. The last application window was 4–15 May; watch the page for the 2027 window.

en: Fully funded, including accommodation and meals at KAUST
No GPA or English test minimum
Prepares for graduate admissions and STEM careers

eligibility.en: Saudi women in their final undergraduate year or fresh graduates with a STEM bachelor's degree.

en: Watch the Women in STEM page for the May 2027 window
Submit the online application form
Take the STEM and English admissions test
Attend the personal interview

costs.en: Free; accommodation and meals covered during in-person periods.

score_reason: Fully funded but Saudi women only; next window ~May 2027.

about.en:
Tech Generation is a Mawhiba programme that develops technology skills among gifted students identified through the National Program for Gifted Identification. Nominated students choose a course and attend either in person or remotely.

It is open to Saudi students from the third year of intermediate school to the third year of secondary school who hold the required score on the Mawhiba Multiple Mental Abilities Test (MMCAT). Registration is done through the Mawhiba services system.

The guardian contribution is 115 SAR for in-person and 57.5 SAR for remote attendance (VAT included). Registration ends on 10 November 2026.

Very low cost (57.5–115 SAR)

about.en:
The Mawhiba Academic Enrichment Program is a summer programme that builds scientific knowledge, practical skills and personal skills, preparing students for Mawhiba's advanced local and international programmes. The 2026 edition ran in July for three weeks: an in-person commuter format (15 days, ~60 hours) at host organisations in several cities, or an online format (45 hours) on Mawhiba's e-learning platform.

Tracks cover medical/biological/chemical sciences, physical/earth/space sciences, engineering and architecture, and computer science/applied maths/economics, with activities, projects and a closing showcase. A certificate requires 80% attendance.

It is open to students in the National Program for Gifted Identification in grades 3–11 who meet the MMCAT thresholds (1355–1400 depending on level). Saudi students and children of Saudi mothers are eligible; non-Saudis can make up to 10% of places. 2026 fees ranged from 460 to 2,300 SAR.

en: In-person in several cities or fully online
Four science and engineering tracks

about.en:
The Mawhiba Research Enrichment Program introduces high-potential students to real scientific research. Working with specialists at partner universities, hospitals and research institutes, students do hands-on lab work and learn research methods and ethics; full-time, part-time and (where available) online formats are offered.

The 2026 session ran 5–30 July 2026 with registration from 2 February to 18 May 2026, so the 2027 cycle is expected on a similar timeline.

Saudi nationals or children of Saudi mothers are eligible; non-Saudis up to 10%. 2026 fees were 3,000 SAR full-time and 1,750 SAR part-time, with discounts and waivers for some groups.

Applicants must be Level 3 (grades 9–11) in the National Program for Gifted Identification with an MMCAT score of 1400+ and, if the test was taken in Arabic, a minimum English score (e.g. IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL iBT 53). Saudi nationals or children of Saudi mothers are eligible; non-Saudis up to 10%.

about.en:
The Mawhiba International Olympiad Program prepares Saudi students for international science olympiads (IMO, IPhO, IChO, IBO, IOI, IJSO, IOAA). Students nominated from the National Gifted Olympiad (Scientific Track) progress through a First Elite Camp, a Second Elite Camp held each November, further camps and an intensive training phase of 30–60 days at KAUST, coordinated with the Ministry of Education.

Each camp lasts about two weeks and ends with an exam; only students who pass continue. Attendance of at least 80% is required for a certificate.

It is for Saudi nationals in grades 8–12. The way in is to register for the National Gifted Olympiad and pass its qualification stages.

about.en:
The Misk Fellowship is a hybrid, English-language leadership accelerator that aims to discover, develop and connect high-potential Saudi youth leaders. Over six months fellows complete a leadership bootcamp, compete on UN SDG-related challenges facing Saudi Arabia, receive one-to-one coaching and attend leadership masterclasses and professional development modules, with activities both in Saudi Arabia and abroad.

It is open to Saudi bachelor's, master's and PhD students (any major, no age limit) who are enrolled at or admitted to a top international university, show leadership potential and commit to all mandatory events and to community service.

The programme is free; Misk covers flights, accommodation and training for international activities. Selection is by Misk Hub application, an online psychometric test and a virtual interview.

Insurance Barmajan is the Insurance Authority's hackathon within its innovation ecosystem. Teams build solutions for the Saudi insurance sector over three days (12–14 November 2026) at The Garage in Riyadh, across four tracks covering customer experience, digital services, AI and data, embedded and on-demand insurance, and insurance for major events and mass gatherings.

It is open to university students, developers and technical specialists, innovators, entrepreneurs, startups, insurtech companies and sector experts. Winners are honoured at the ingate 2026 conference (16–18 November).

Prizes total SAR 560,000: per track SAR 80,000 / 40,000 / 20,000 for first to third place, plus seats in incubation and acceleration programmes; every applicant gets access to a digital-tools perks platform. Register by 7 November 2026.

Kangaroo Mawhiba is the Saudi edition of the worldwide Kangaroo mathematics competition, which rewards logical thinking and problem solving rather than advanced syllabus knowledge. Mawhiba runs it remotely on an online platform; students receive login details by email and sit the exam at the time set for their grade band.

In 2026, registration ran 2 February – 7 April, a trial test was offered 8–13 April, exams took place 17–18 April by grade band (primary grades 3–6, intermediate and secondary), and results came out on 28 April. Medals are delivered through Talent Management departments of the education directorates.

It is a low-stakes, free way for Saudi school students to try a recognised international competition and a common first step towards Mawhiba's olympiad programmes.

Startup Blueprint is Sheraa's entry-level programme for people who want to turn an idea into a business. It is delivered online (80 lessons, about 2.5 hours of video) with a hybrid community layer of in-person meetups and AMA sessions with mentors in Sharjah.

Twelve chapters cover problem definition, design thinking and Lean Canvas, legal basics, startup finance and cap tables, market sizing, fundraising, founder leadership, hiring, MVP and product, sales and customer discovery, marketing and pitching. Quizzes run throughout and completers receive a certificate.

It is free and open to anyone; graduates are evaluated for a validation bootcamp and Sheraa's Sharjah Startup Studio (S3) accelerator.

Over four weeks (29 November – 24 December 2026) at CODED's campus in Kuwait's Free Trade Zone, participants build an AI secretary connected to real tools, an AI finance manager (document extraction, n8n workflows, reconciliation and reporting), an AI customer agent (WhatsApp Business API, lead scoring, multi-agent hand-offs) and a capstone 'AI department' presented at Demo Day.

about.en:
The International Kangaroo Science Competition (IKSC) tests how well students reason with everyday and basic scientific ideas; there is no fixed syllabus. It is a 120-minute multiple-choice paper in five categories: Pre-Ecolier (Grades 1–2), Ecolier (3–4), Benjamin (5–6), Cadet (7–8) and Junior (9–10).

The UAE round is run by ThinkTanks. Registration is open 3 August – 2 November 2026, confirmations go out on 12 November, the contest is held at schools on 30 November 2026 and results are due 30 December 2026.

The fee is AED 150 per student; school registration is free.

about.en:
Middlesex University Dubai runs a Winter Camp for school students during the December break, 14–18 December 2026, 9 am–6 pm daily. Mornings are specialist workshops and discovery sessions in subjects such as business, computer engineering, fashion, media and law, plus academic-skills workshops and a campus tour; afternoons are team-building games and activities, with optional excursions.

It is a low-pressure way to sample university subjects and campus life in Dubai before choosing a degree. International visitors can contact the camp team for arrangements.

The fee is AED 1,700 for the week (excursions extra). Register via the apply option on the camp page or by contacting the team.

about.en:
AUD's pre-university Summer Camp gives Grade 10–11 (Year 11–12) students a taste of university life in Dubai. Students choose one track: Empowered Leadership; Tech Pioneers (AI, game design, robotics and VR); Master the Power of Media; Life-Lab (biology and pre-med); or Creative Lab (design and branding with AI).

The fee covers accommodation, meals, excursions, local transport, modules, on-campus activities and some airport transfers, so it suits international students; insurance, visas and flights are not included. 2027 dates are to be announced.

Apply with your preferred track, country, grade, latest report card and passport copy; AUD then sends next steps and pricing.
